intelligence.human_view: Three laws in one look at the month view. First, no object ever covers a word: the diamond in the headliner pill overlays into the button and covers part of "Tuesday" — a real object never sits on top of letters, so it gets repositioned until no letter is covered. Second, the clock stops being one color and becomes live tiles: Dashboard digit tiles, dynamic, the numbers the show, the color circulating with the hour — 9 magenta, 10 red, 2 orange — the time just the time, no GMT-8, separated a little from the date, AM/PM in the same tile blocks. Why should the clock be one color? It shouldn't. Third, the weekday row stops being words with little diamonds above them and becomes real objects: black obsidian in the middle, bold white letters, the day's own color lighting up on the outside as rim + glow — the PTS/%/MONEY anatomy, the best buttons in the system, applied to Sun through Sat. And the headliner weekday stays white: he first says you'd want Tuesday to be gold, then revises in the same breath — how it is is actually nice, leave it, the white-on-gold contrast is good. The revision is the decision. This ruling is about the month view headliner he was looking at; the day-screen headliner's day-colored weekday (SN-3109/3110) is not what he was looking at and is not changed by this dictation. The honest tension to keep: the v14 checker passed the weekday row on render (Sun–Sat, straight words, diamond above each, nothing clipped) — his eye says it does not look good at all, it is just not pleasing. The checker's fit-pass and his eye disagree; his eye is ground truth, and the row gets rebuilt as objects.
